# Preface {.unnumbered}

These are the lecture notes for ASTRO 442, an introduction to the fluid dynamics and magnetohydrodynamics of astrophysical systems. They are written to be self-contained: the textbook, Clarke and Carswell's *Principles of Astrophysical Fluid Dynamics* [@clarke2007], is optional further reading. Each chapter ends with pointers to the relevant sections of the textbook.

::: {.callout-note}
The notes are being prepared for the Spring 2027 semester. Chapters marked "in preparation" will be completed before the corresponding lecture; see the [Schedule](schedule.qmd).
:::

## How to use these notes {.unnumbered}

- **One chapter per lecture topic.** The [Schedule](schedule.qmd) lists which chapter goes with each lecture.
- **Everything is numbered by chapter.** Equation (9.14) is the fourteenth numbered equation of Chapter 9, and Exercise 8.4 is the fourth exercise of Chapter 8. When you ask a question about the notes, quote these numbers.
- **In-class worksheets** appear near the end of each chapter, followed by the **exercises**. Homework assignments on Canvas list the exercises to solve, for example "Exercises 2.1, 7.3".
- **Optional material** is set apart in boxes titled "Going further"; you can skip it on a first reading.

## Accessibility {.unnumbered}

These notes are designed to meet the Web Content Accessibility Guidelines (WCAG) 2.1, level AA. Mathematics is rendered with MathJax, which supports screen readers, speech, and braille, and lets you explore an equation term by term: click on an equation or focus it with the keyboard, then use the arrow keys. Every figure has a text description.

If something in these notes is not accessible to you, please let me know.
